messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: P1 - serving-cluster-prod. Multiple runtime pods restarting after repeated CUDA/Xid and NCCL timeouts. Auto-escalation to incidents channel. Link: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/2654321000
neha: oncall here, pulling logs and paging eng-runtime and eng-ml. assigning to @kyle and @ajay.
kyle: on it. quick ask — how many nodes/pods?
ajay: seeing spikes in 5 pods across 3 machines, TP4 shards for model redwood-v1. Customer-facing errors: ~504/timeouts and truncated responses.
neha: collecting logs now. command I ran: ```kubectl -n serving logs -l app=redwood -c runtime --since=15m | tail -n 200```
raj: grabbing dmesg + nvml: ```ssh gpu-17 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 80' && nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERRPSTATE```
neha: pasted relevant lines from runtime logs: ```[2026-03-15T21:09:12Z] E runtime: cudaErrorLaunchFailure: kernel aborted (xid=79)
[2026-03-15T21:09:13Z] W nccl: NCCL WARN TIMEOUT in comm 0x7f8b2c.. waiting ring stall
[2026-03-15T21:09:13Z] E runtime: communicator stuck, attempting soft reset
[2026-03-15T21:09:14Z] E runtime: process restarted (OOM? exit code 137)```
kyle: looks like a livelock where NCCL allreduce stalls -> processes spin then one OOMs/restarts. Could be a driver/GPU firmware flake or intermittent PCIe error. Immediate mitigations: (1) drain the flapping node(s), (2) shift traffic to single-GPU fallback model, (3) disable P2P NCCL paths as temporary env override.
kyle: drain command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-17 && kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 -n serving```
kyle: env patch for disabling P2P (runtime): ```kubectl set env deploy/redwood-runtime NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=0 -n serving```
raj: starting drain on gpu-17 now. ```kubectl drain gpu-17...``` pods are rescheduling. saw one pod restart with OOMKill during eviction.
ops-bot: Deploy rollback started by neha: route redwood-v1 -> redwood-v1-slim canary 10% at 2654321234
neha: canary tests: ```curl -sS https://api.redwood.example/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq .'``` smoke requests show tokens streaming, latency normal for v1-slim.
ajay: observed customer error_rate: peak 6.8% at 21:08 -> after canary to v1-slim error_rate down to 1.1% in 5m. traffic shifted to 100% at 2654321298 :white_check_mark:
kyle: left NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=0 for now. if stability holds for 30m we'll revert and repro on isolated node. need heap/dump + nvml logs for the OOM'd container.
neha: collecting debug artifacts: ```kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/redwood-runtime-abc -- bash -c 'mkdir /tmp/diag && cp /var/log/runtime/*.log /tmp/diag && tar -czf /tmp/diag.tgz /tmp/diag'``` and uploading to s3://redwood-incident-archives/2654321000/
raj: dmesg from gpu-17 shows repeated PCIe link resets then Xid 79 entries — attaching snippet. suspect intermittent HW link flaps.
kyle: good catch. plan: (A) keep drained node out of rotation, (B) keep P2P disabled across runtime pools for 1h, (C) postmortem + vendor escalation if HW flaps confirmed.
neha: notifying support & affected customers with temporary mitigation summary and ETA for full root cause (TBD). adding incident tag P1 and assigning follow-ups to @raj (node repro & HW triage) and @kyle (runtime mitigations & revert plan).
sre-bot: Incident recorded: 2654321000 - assigned: neha, kyle, raj. status: mitigated -> traffic shifted to fallback variant; monitoring.
ajay: monitoring user-facing metrics in datadog: throughput restored to baseline, queue depth back to normal, tail latency acceptable. will validate prompts/quality differences vs v1.
neha: opening postmortem ticket and collecting artifacts. next steps: hardware vendor request for pci-e logs, runtime heap dumps, and a controlled repro job on an isolated node. will update channel when vendor responds. :eyes:
kyle: if we see recurrence after revert we'll escalate to infra-oncall for hardware replacement. Otherwise we'll schedule rollback of NCCL env change and controlled canary for 1.0 at 2h post-mitigation.
neha: closing page for now — keeping channel open for follow-ups. final note: avoid rolling many TP shards onto a single node until we have HW verdict. :white_check_mark:
